standard.title: Prefixes, suffixes and word families
standard.description: build morphemic word families using knowledge of prefixes and suffixes
standard.prior_knowledge: Students use grammatical morphemes to create and recognise word families (AC9E1LY15). They have not yet systematically built word families using a range of named prefixes and suffixes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can build morphemic word families using knowledge of prefixes and suffixes.

nodes.label: What prefixes and suffixes do
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain that prefixes and suffixes change the meaning or grammatical function of a base word and give at least one example of each.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify a prefix or suffix on a given word and explain what it adds to the base word (e.g. 'un-' changes meaning; '-ing' changes tense).
nodes.typical_width: Identify prefixes and suffixes across a range of words, explain what each adds, and distinguish between meaning-changing prefixes (un-, re-) and grammatical suffixes (-ing, -ed, -er, -est).
wider: Compare words with the same prefix or suffix across multiple examples and discuss what pattern of meaning the prefix/suffix creates
Identify prefixes and suffixes encountered in learning area vocabulary and discuss how knowing the affix helps with word meaning

response_modes.reason: Students often think 'un-' or '-ing' are just part of the word, not added elements. Multiple examples across different base words — showing that the same prefix changes different base words in the same way — resolves the misconception that affixes are arbitrary. More base word examples, not more explanation of one, is productive.

nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding that prefixes and suffixes are separable, meaningful elements is conceptually prerequisite for Node 2 — students who see affixes as arbitrary word-parts cannot systematically build word families by adding or removing them.
success_criteria: Student can identify a prefix or suffix and name the base word.
Student can explain what the prefix or suffix adds to the base word's meaning or grammatical function.

nodes.label: Building word families
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can build a word family from a base word by adding prefixes and suffixes, producing correctly spelled related words.
nodes.minimum_width: Build at least three words in a family from a known base word using prefixes or suffixes (e.g. 'friend' → 'friendly', 'friendship', 'unfriendly').
nodes.typical_width: Build word families from several base words, applying prefixes and suffixes correctly; use morphemic knowledge to write unknown words by analogy with known family members.
wider: Use a known word family to write unknown words encountered during reading or writing across subject areas
Compare word families with the same base word built using different affixes (e.g. 'cover', 'uncover', 'covering', 'recover', 'discovery') and map the family structure

response_modes.reason: Building word families requires accumulating examples — each new base word and its family members adds to the student's morphemic vocabulary. Schema for how prefixes and suffixes work only forms once a sufficient range of examples has been encountered. Breadth of base words is the productive investment.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Mapping complex word families — where multiple prefixes and suffixes apply to the same base — is genuinely rich for advancing students. It connects morphology to vocabulary development and spelling, and the 'discovery' family example shows how family trees can be complex and generative.
success_criteria: Student correctly builds at least three words in a family from a known base word.
Student correctly spells the words in the family, including words formed by combining the base with both a prefix and a suffix.
